1. `SystemAudioClassifier.startAnalyzing` (GlobalDetection/SystemAudioClassifier.swift:820-861) is dispatched entirely from `DispatchQueue.global(qos: .userInitiated)` and calls `configureBackgroundAudioSession()` at the end, but `configureBackgroundAudioSession()` manipulates UIKit/foreground APIs (`UIApplication.shared.beginBackgroundTask`/`endBackgroundTask`, creating background timers, configuring `AVAudioSession`) and is not bound to the main thread (`GlobalDetection/SystemAudioClassifier.swift:689-724`). As soon as detection starts (the normal app launch path), the Main Thread Checker will report “UI API called on a background thread: UIApplication”; in release builds this is undefined behavior and can crash if UIApplication internally asserts, preventing any background tasks from being registered. Impact: detection cannot start reliably because the background-task plumbing runs off‑main. Repro: enable detection and watch the console in a debug build with Main Thread Checker enabled—the stack will point to `configureBackgroundAudioSession` being invoked from the global queue that started `startAnalyzing`.

2. `pauseAudioEngine(…)` asynchronously deactivates `AVAudioSession` (`setActive(false)`) on `DispatchQueue.global` (GlobalDetection/SystemAudioClassifier.swift:333-363) while `resumeAudioEngine(…)` concurrently runs `startAudioSession()`/`setActive(true)` on a different background queue before the first call has finished (GlobalDetection/SystemAudioClassifier.swift:366-446). Because `AVAudioSession.setActive(_)` is not reentrant, this race can deliver `AVAudioSessionError`/`kAudioSessionAlreadyActiveError` and leave the classifier stuck after a quick pause/resume cycle (e.g., TTS in `convotab` posts `PauseAudioEngine` then `ResumeAudioEngine` 0.3s later). Impact: rapid conversation/TTS transitions or user toggles can prevent detection from resuming, trigger OS warnings, or even crash due to overlapping audio-session state changes. Repro: start the speech UI that invokes `PauseAudioEngine`/`ResumeAudioEngine` (see `convotab/TextView.swift` around 2068 and `SpeechRecognitionManager.swift:262`, 621); while the 0.3s pause is in flight, the two `setActive` calls collide and you’ll see `AVAudioSession` errors in the log and detection never restarts.

Next steps:
1. Guard `configureBackgroundAudioSession()` (and any calls to `UIApplication.shared`) so it always executes on the main thread before `startAnalyzing` finishes.
2. Serialize the `AVAudioSession.setActive`/`startAudioSession` paths (e.g., a dedicated serial queue or `@MainActor`) so pause and resume cannot overlap and race the audio session state.
